title: You Think Beginners Rate Themselves Above Experts, Yet Cornell Proved the Opposite
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — David Dunning & Justin Kruger (1999): Metacognitive Blindness & the Real Shape of the 'Mount Stupid' Myth, grounded in Justin Kruger, David Dunning (1999) (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology). Empirical findings show that in 1995 in Pittsburgh, McArthur Wheeler robbed two banks in broad daylight with zero mask — shocked upon arrest because he thought rubbing LEMON JUICE ('invisible ink') on his skin made his face invisible to security cameras.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: Reading that news clipping at Cornell, David Dunning and graduate student Justin Kruger realized a deep cognitive double-curse (1999): in many intellectual skills, the exact knowledge needed to PRODUCE a right answer is the exact same knowledge needed to RECOGNIZE a wrong answer.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Justin Kruger, David Dunning (1999). Unskilled and unaware of it: How difficulties in recognizing one's own incompetence lead to inflated self-assessments. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.77.6.1121
- David Oliver (2022). David Oliver: Covid-19 and the Dunning-Kruger effect. BMJ. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.o1701
- Corey S. Powell, David Dunning, Corey S. Powell (2026). David Dunning : « L’effet Dunning-Kruger nous touche tous un jour ou l’autre ». Cerveau & Psycho. https://doi.org/10.3917/cerpsy.186.0060
